gen-gf-oxanium-gf-carrois-gothic: Carrois Gothic reads modern and businesslike, with a high-set x-height and generously opened curves. And Oxanium, drawn in one unbroken monoline stroke, brings the commanding display edge that the body font quietly leaves alone.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-chivo:
Oxanium's monoline strokes give it a distinctive, commanding edge.

Chivo keeps its lowercase packed up toward the capitals, with daylight showing through every curve, so paragraphs of it feel approachable and steady instead of tiring.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-cossette-texte: Oxanium's big lowercase and curves that end in clear daylight give the heading a commanding, distinctive look on the page. Cossette Texte, wide-eyed in its e, follows quietly.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Loud, loose and friendly. Grandstander has no hairlines to squint at when it shrinks. Noto Sans Old Hungarian handles the quieter work, keeping its big open counters clear even at tiny sizes.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Noto Sans Old Italic sits low, with very little gap between x-height and cap height and curve endings kept well apart. Grandstander beside it brings bold, plain lines with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-old-nor: Approachable is the mood here, with Grandstander's bold, plain lines held open instead of curled shut. Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense band of lowercase with outward-pointing terminals, so a long page feels steady and compact.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-old-tur: Approachable and clean, this pairing sets Grandstander's bold, unshaded line, which never swells, beside chunky lowercase with open-mouthed curves. Grandstander is best at making a statement; Noto Sans Old Turkic is best at staying clear.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-osage: Grandstander builds its letters like bent tubing, the same gauge from start to finish, bold and expressive in every curve. Noto Sans Osage adds inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that never close up.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-saurash: Grandstander's bold letters never thicken or thin anywhere along the stroke. They work best large and short, while Noto Sans Saurashtra keeps its counters open to the outside and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-sc: Rounded, bold, cord-like lines. Grandstander is the loud one here, while Noto Sans SC lets chalky curves stop well before closing, so a long page of it reads in a modern, quiet way.
